definition_en: a farm bird kept for its eggs and meat, the meat of this bird, or a timid person
core_image: 院子里低头啄食的母鸡
scene: 清晨的院子里传来咯咯的叫声。A hen and her chickens scratched the ground near the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 chicken 指「鸡」（第 1 个义项：为蛋和肉饲养的家禽）；句意是一只母鸡带着小鸡在门边刨地。

senses.title: The farm bird
senses.definition: a farm bird with feathers and wings, kept for its eggs and meat
senses.definitionCN: 长着羽毛和翅膀、为取蛋和肉而饲养的家禽
senses.example: The chickens ran across the yard at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天刚亮，鸡就跑过院子。
senses.why: The Old English word meant a young fowl, and it later covered the adult bird.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指幼禽，后来扩展到成鸟。

senses.title: The meat as food
senses.definition: the meat of this bird, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 这种鸟可供食用的肉
senses.example: We had roast chicken for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚餐吃了烤鸡。
senses.why: English often uses the animal name for its meat when the meat is bought and cooked.
senses.whyCN: 英语常直接用动物名指其肉，尤其是买来烹饪的肉。

senses.title: A timid person
senses.definition: a person who is easily frightened or afraid to take a risk
senses.definitionCN: 容易害怕或不敢冒险的人
senses.example: He called me a chicken for refusing the jump.
senses.exampleCN: 因为我不敢跳，他叫我胆小鬼。
senses.why: The bird's nervous fluttering made its name a mild insult for cowardice.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟容易惊慌扑腾，名字便被用来轻微讥讽怯懦。

intro.en: Chicken began as the word for a young fowl and grew to cover the whole bird.
intro.cn: chicken 起初指幼禽，后来扩展到指整只家禽。

items.en: Kiukinam named a young fowl.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kiukinam 指幼禽。

items.en: Cicen named a chick or a young hen.
items.cn: 古英语 cicen 指小鸡或小母鸡。

items.en: Chiken widened to the adult farm bird.
items.cn: 中古英语 chiken 扩展到成年的家禽。

items.en: The word also named the meat served at table.
items.cn: 这个词也指端上餐桌的鸡肉。

items.en: A chicken can now be a bird, a dish or a coward.
items.cn: 如今 chicken 可以是鸟、一道菜，也可以是胆小鬼。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and -en shape, while the meaning group names birds and cowards.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与 -en 的形态，近义组列出鸟类与怯懦者。

entries.definition: the room where food is cooked
a baby bird, especially a young chicken
a common illness with red spots
entries.definitionCN: 长红色斑点的一种常见病

entries.definition: an adult female chicken
farm birds kept for eggs and meat
entries.definitionCN: 为取蛋和肉饲养的家禽

entries.definition: a person who lacks courage

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the young-bird origin, the meat sense and the coward sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「幼禽」来源、鸡肉义以及胆小鬼义。

normal.en: Chicken first meant a chick, and the small word grew up with the bird.
normal.cn: chicken 起初指小鸡，这个小词跟着鸟一起长大。

normal.en: The plural chickens counts live birds, while the meat stays uncountable.
normal.cn: 复数 chickens 数的是活鸡，而鸡肉义不可数。

normal.en: Chicken out means to lose courage at the last moment.
normal.cn: chicken out 意为在最后一刻失去勇气。

normal.en: Chick, chicken and chickenpox all start from the same small bird.
normal.cn: chick、chicken、chickenpox 都从同一种小鸟出发。

normal.en: Fried chicken and chicken soup are the two phrases a menu repeats.
normal.cn: fried chicken 与 chicken soup 是菜单上反复出现的两个搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a hen's head dipping and rising in the dust.
abstract.cn: 想象母鸡的头在尘土里一低一抬。

abstract.en: Picture a plate of golden chicken fresh from the oven.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘刚出炉的金黄鸡肉。

abstract.en: Picture someone stepping back from a diving board.
abstract.cn: 想象有人从跳板边退回一步。

examples.en: The farmer keeps chickens and two goats.
examples.cn: 农场主养鸡，还养了两只山羊。

examples.en: She added chicken to the soup at the end.
examples.cn: 她最后把鸡肉加进了汤里。

examples.en: He wanted to ask her out but chickened out.
examples.cn: 他想约她，却临阵退缩了。

dict_mnemonic.text: chick 是小鸡，chicken 加长了仍是鸡；吓得像小鸡一样扑腾的人，就是胆小鬼。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kiukinam（幼禽），古英语作 cicen，中古英语 chiken 扩展为家禽，后又指鸡肉与怯懦者。

sensesIntro.en: The young bird grows into the farm bird, the table borrows the bird's name for its meat, and the bird's panic gives the insult.
sensesIntro.cn: 幼禽长成家禽，餐桌借鸟名指其肉，而鸟的惊慌又给出骂人的义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small farm bird pecking at the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在地上一啄一啄的小家禽。

branches.en: The living bird runs in the yard.
branches.cn: 活着的鸡在院子里跑。

branches.en: The meat sense fills the plate.
branches.cn: 鸡肉义项装满盘子。

branches.en: The insult sense names a fearful person.
branches.cn: 讥讽义项指胆小的人。

branches.en: Bird and meat share one word on menus.
branches.cn: 鸟与肉在菜单上共用一个词。

branches.en: The bird's fluttering becomes the image of fear.
branches.cn: 鸟的扑腾成了恐惧的意象。

intro.en: Chicken keeps one short stem through its plural and its two compounds.
intro.cn: chicken 在复数与两个复合词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the closest old forms are cicen and kiukinam.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，最接近的古形式是 cicen 与 kiukinam。

items.meaning: a farm bird or its meat
items.example: The chicken is in the oven.
The chickens were fed at six.
A chick broke out of the shell.

items.meaningCN: 儿童常见的长斑点疾病

items.example: The word coward matches the third sense.
items.exampleCN: coward 一词对应第三个义项。

items.example: Kiukinam is the oldest known form.
items.exampleCN: kiukinam 是已知最古老的形式。

latinEntries.example: Kiukinam became Old English cicen.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kiukinam 变成古英语的 cicen。

definition_zh: 首领；酋长；主要的；首席的
definition_en: the leader of a group or an organization, or most important and highest in rank
core_image: 站在队伍最前面的那个人
scene: 会议桌两端坐满了人，屋里渐渐安静。The chief of the village spoke last and everyone listened.
sceneCN: 这里 chief 指「首领」（第 1 个义项：群体或组织的领导者）；句意是村里的首领最后发言，所有人都在听。

senses.title: The leader of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a group, a tribe or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导群体、部落或组织的人
senses.example: The village chief settled the dispute himself.
senses.exampleCN: 村长亲自解决了这场争端。
senses.why: The Latin word for head gave the name of the person at the head of a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「头」的词，给出了站在一群人最前面那个人的称呼。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: most important among several things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中最重要的
senses.example: The chief reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: The head is the top of the body, so the adjective came to mean topmost in importance.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的顶端，因此形容词表示重要性上位居最高。

senses.title: Highest in rank
senses.definition: holding the highest position in a profession or an office
senses.definitionCN: 在某行业或机构中居于最高职位的
senses.example: She was appointed chief engineer of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为该项目的总工程师。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as height, so the head word marks the top post in a title.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高低，因此这个「头」词标记出头衔中的最高职位。

intro.en: Chief is the Latin word for head, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: chief 是拉丁语中表示「头」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Caput meant the head of a person or an animal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 指人或动物的头。

items.en: Chief meant the head, both of a body and of a group.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 既指身体的头，也指群体的头。

items.en: Chief named the leading person of a household or a band.
items.cn: 英语 chief 指家庭或队伍中的领头人。

items.en: The same form began to work as an adjective meaning principal.
items.cn: 同一形式开始作形容词，意为首要的。

items.en: Chief covers leaders, top posts and the most important reason.
items.cn: 如今 chief 涵盖首领、最高职位与最重要的理由。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same long vowel or the same origin, while the meaning group names leaders.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的长元音或同一来源，近义组列出领导者。

entries.definition: the head cook of a kitchen
a person who steals
a community ruled by a chief
a person who guides a group
the person in charge of a group
the most important of several things

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root caput, the chef doublet and the rank sense of chief.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根 caput、同源词 chef 以及 chief 的职位义。

normal.en: Chief and chef are twins: the French form became the cook, the English one the leader.
normal.cn: chief 与 chef 是一对双胞胎：法语形式成了厨师，英语形式成了首领。

normal.en: Chief hides caput, the Latin head, also seen in capital and captain.
normal.cn: chief 里藏着拉丁语「头」caput，capital 与 captain 也含这个词根。

normal.en: A chief is at the head of people; a chief reason is at the head of a list.
normal.cn: chief 是人前的头，也是理由清单上的头。

normal.en: The plural chiefs simply adds an s after two consonants.
normal.cn: 复数 chiefs 只需在词尾加 s。

normal.en: Editor in chief puts the head word after the job, a common newspaper title.
normal.cn: editor in chief 把「头」词放在职务之后，是常见的报纸头衔。

abstract.en: Picture one figure standing a step ahead of a long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在长队前面半步。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to quiet a whole hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，让整个大厅安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate reading chief engineer on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一块写着总工程师的名牌。

examples.en: The chief called the meeting to order.
examples.cn: 首领宣布会议开始。

examples.en: Safety is our chief concern.
examples.cn: 安全是我们最主要的关切。

examples.en: He was chief of the department for ten years.
examples.cn: 他担任该部门主管十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: chief 与 chef 同源，都是「头」：厨房的头是主厨，人群的头是首领。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经古法语 chief 进入英语，既作名词「首领」，也作形容词「首要的」。

sensesIntro.en: The head of a body of people gives the leader, and the head as the topmost part gives both the important and the highest-ranked senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 一群人中的「头」给出首领义，而作为最顶端的「头」给出「主要」与「最高职位」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head of a body, human or social.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体或一个群体的「头」。

branches.en: The leader sense names a person.
branches.cn: 首领义项指一个人。

branches.en: The important sense ranks reasons and aims.
branches.cn: 主要义项给理由与目标排序。

branches.en: The rank sense builds titles such as chief engineer.
branches.cn: 职位义项构成总工程师这类头衔。

branches.en: A chief holds the chief post.
branches.cn: 首领占据最高的职位。

branches.en: Both adjective senses place something at the top.
branches.cn: 两个形容词义项都把某物置于顶端。

intro.en: Chief builds a small family from the Latin head root caput.
intro.cn: chief 从拉丁语「头」词根 caput 出发，构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput, the head, also gives capital, captain and the French chef.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput（头）也给出 capital、captain 以及法语的 chef。

items.example: The land is chiefly used for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用来放牧。

items.example: The chieftain wore a heavy cloak.

items.meaning: a society led by a chief
the leader of a team or a ship

items.exampleCN: caput 是 chief 背后的词。

latinEntries.example: Caput became Old French chief.
latinEntries.exampleCN: caput 变成古法语 chief。

definition_en: a young human being, or a son or daughter of any age
core_image: 牵着大人手的小小身影
scene: 公园长椅旁，一个小身影蹲下来看地面。The child watched the ants for almost an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 child 指「儿童」（第 1 个义项：年幼的人）；句意是那个孩子看蚂蚁看了将近一小时。

senses.title: A young person
senses.definition: a human being who is not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 尚未成年的人
senses.example: Every child in the class received a book.
senses.exampleCN: 班上每个孩子都得到了一本书。
senses.why: The Old English word named a young person, and that sense has stayed at the centre.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指年幼的人，这一义项始终居于中心。

senses.title: A son or daughter
senses.definition: a son or a daughter of any age, seen from the parent's side
senses.definitionCN: 从父母角度看，任何年龄的儿子或女儿
senses.example: They have three children, all grown up.
senses.exampleCN: 他们有三个孩子，都已成年。
senses.why: A parent's relation to offspring lasts for life, so the word ignores age.
senses.whyCN: 父母与子女的关系终身存在，因此这个词不再管年龄。

senses.title: A product of its time
senses.definition: something that is produced by a particular period or influence
senses.definitionCN: 由某个时期或某种影响产生的事物
senses.example: The novel is a child of the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是上个世纪的产物。
senses.why: Something produced is pictured as born, so child became a metaphor for a product.
senses.whyCN: 被产生出来的东西被想象成「出生」，于是 child 成了产物的比喻。

intro.en: Child is an old English word, and its plural children is an old double plural.
intro.cn: child 是一个古英语词，复数 children 则是古老的双重复数。

items.en: A root kel- named the womb and the young born from it.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kel- 指子宫以及由它生出的幼者。

items.en: Cild meant a fetus or a young person.
items.cn: 古英语 cild 指胎儿或年幼的人。

items.en: The plural cildru appeared beside the singular.
items.cn: 复数形式 cildru 与单数形式并存。

items.en: Children added -en to an older plural, a double plural.
items.cn: children 在旧复数后加了 -en，形成双重复数。

items.en: Child covers young people, offspring of any age and products of a period.
items.cn: 如今 child 涵盖儿童、任何年龄的子女以及某个时期的产物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and -ild shape, while the meaning group names young people.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与 -ild 的形态，近义组列出年幼的人。

entries.definition: a cold feeling or a mild illness
to speak to someone in disapproval
the period of being a child
an informal word for a child
a very young baby
the children of a person or an animal

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the odd plural children, the -hood relative and the product metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用特殊复数 children、-hood 派生词以及「产物」的比喻。

normal.en: Child has one of the strangest plurals in English: children hides an old double plural.
normal.cn: child 的复数在英语里格外特别：children 里藏着古老的双重复数。

normal.en: Childhood adds -hood, the same ending as in adulthood and neighbourhood.
normal.cn: childhood 加 -hood，与 adulthood、neighbourhood 用同一个词尾。

normal.en: Childish is negative, childlike is positive: one is silly, the other innocent.
normal.cn: childish 带贬义，childlike 带褒义：一个指幼稚，一个指天真。

normal.en: An only child has no brothers or sisters at all.
normal.cn: an only child 指完全没有兄弟姐妹的孩子。

normal.en: Calling a novel a child of its age means the age produced it.
normal.cn: 把小说称作某个时代的 child，意思就是那个时代产生了它。

abstract.en: Picture a small hand held inside a much larger one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小手被一只大得多的手握着。

abstract.en: Picture a face level with the grass, watching ants.
abstract.cn: 想象一张与草地齐平的脸在看蚂蚁。

abstract.en: Picture school shoes lined up at a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一双双校鞋在门口排好。

examples.en: The child fell asleep on the bus.
examples.cn: 那个孩子在公交车上睡着了。

examples.en: She is the youngest child in the family.
examples.cn: 她是家里最小的孩子。

examples.en: This custom is a child of the sea trade.
examples.cn: 这一习俗是海上贸易的产物。

dict_mnemonic.text: child 的复数是 children：一个人是 child，一群孩子就成了 children。

root: 源自古英语 cild（胎儿、幼者），属日耳曼语词根 kel-（子宫、幼者），复数 children 由旧复数再加 -en 构成。

sensesIntro.en: A young person is the core sense, the parent's view extends it to any age, and something produced is pictured as born.
sensesIntro.cn: 年幼的人是核心义，父母的视角把它扩展到任何年龄，而被产生之物又被想象成出生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small figure whose hand is held by an adult.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被大人牵着手的小小身影。

branches.en: The young-person sense is the everyday one.
branches.cn: 儿童义项是日常最常用的。

branches.en: The offspring sense ignores age entirely.
branches.cn: 子女义项完全不看年龄。

branches.en: The metaphor sense describes works and ideas.
branches.cn: 比喻义项用来描述作品与观念。

branches.en: A child is both a young person and someone's son or daughter.
branches.cn: 一个孩子既是年幼的人，也是某人的子女。

branches.en: Both extend the idea of being produced.
branches.cn: 两者都延伸了「被产生」的意思。

intro.en: Child builds a family with -hood, -ish and -less.
intro.cn: child 与 -hood、-ish、-less 构成一个词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic rather than Latin; its old root named the womb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，其古词根指子宫。

items.example: The child laughed at the puppet.

items.meaning: the time of being a child
items.example: He spent his childhood by the sea.

items.meaning: silly in a way expected of a child
an informal word for a child

latinEntries.meaning: a fetus or a young person
latinEntries.example: Cild is the direct source of child.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cild 是 child 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Cildru grew into children.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cildru 演变成 children。

definition_en: the period of life when a person is a child
core_image: 一张边角卷起的童年合影
scene: 老屋里翻出一本相册，边角已经卷起。Her childhood was spent in a small town by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 childhood 指「童年」（第 1 个义项：身为儿童的时期）；句意是她的童年在河边的一座小镇度过。

senses.title: The time of being a child
senses.definition: the period of a person's life when they are a child
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身为儿童的那段生命时期
senses.example: He spent his childhood on a farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的童年在农场度过。
senses.why: The suffix -hood names a state or a period, so child plus -hood is the time of being a child.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 表示状态或时期，因此 child 加 -hood 就是身为儿童的时期。

senses.title: An early stage of development
senses.definition: the early period in the growth of an idea, an industry or a movement
senses.definitionCN: 某种观念、行业或运动成长中的早期阶段
senses.example: The film industry was still in its childhood then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时电影业还处在萌芽阶段。
senses.why: A young thing passes through a childhood too, so the human period became a metaphor for early growth.
senses.whyCN: 新生事物也会经历「童年」，于是人生的这段时期成了早期发展的比喻。

intro.en: Childhood joins the old word child to the native suffix -hood, which names a state.
intro.cn: childhood 把古词 child 与表示状态的本土后缀 -hood 结合。

items.en: Cild meant a young person.
items.cn: 古英语 cild 指年幼的人。

items.en: The suffix -had named a state or a condition.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -had 表示状态或境况。

items.en: The suffix settled as -hood in words like manhood.
items.cn: 这个后缀在 manhood 等词中定型为 -hood。

items.en: Childhood fixed the sense of the whole period of being young.
items.cn: childhood 固定为「整个年幼时期」的意思。

items.en: The word also describes the early stage of an industry or an idea.
items.cn: 这个词也用来描述行业或观念的早期阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from child, while the meaning group names periods of early life.
note.cn: 形近组由 child 派生，近义组列出生命的早期阶段。

entries.definition: a young person
silly in the way of a child
more than one child
the period when someone is young
the earliest period of life
the time when someone is a boy

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -hood period suffix and the parallel words adulthood and manhood.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示时期的 -hood 后缀以及 adulthood、manhood 这类平行词。

normal.en: Childhood is child plus -hood, the same ending that gives adulthood and manhood.
normal.cn: childhood 是 child 加 -hood，adulthood 与 manhood 也用这个结尾。

normal.en: The suffix -hood names a state or a span of time, never a place.
normal.cn: 后缀 -hood 表示状态或一段时间，从不表示地点。

normal.en: Childhood is uncountable, so you say a happy childhood, not happy childhoods.
normal.cn: childhood 不可数，所以说 a happy childhood，而不用复数。

normal.en: Childhood memories are the scenes that stay after the years go.
normal.cn: childhood memories 是岁月过去后仍留着的画面。

normal.en: An industry in its childhood is young and still experimenting.
normal.cn: 处在 childhood 的行业很年轻，仍在摸索。

abstract.en: Picture a photo album open on a dusty floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一本相册摊在落灰的地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a river town seen from a child's height.
abstract.cn: 想象从孩子的高度看河边小镇。

abstract.en: Picture a small bicycle leaning against a wall for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆小自行车靠墙放了很多年。

examples.en: She had a quiet childhood in the countryside.
examples.cn: 她在乡下度过了安静的童年。

examples.en: Childhood memories of that kitchen still comfort him.
examples.cn: 那间厨房的童年记忆至今让他安心。

examples.en: Electric cars were still in their childhood a decade ago.
examples.cn: 十年前电动汽车还处在萌芽阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: child 加 -hood（表示时期）：当孩子的那些年，就是童年。

root: 由古英语 cild（幼者）加本土后缀 -hood（状态、时期，源自古英语 -had）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix turns a person into a period, and any young thing can borrow that period as a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个后缀把人变成一个时期，而任何新生事物都能借这段时期作比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a span of years seen through a child's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过孩子的眼睛看到的一段岁月。

branches.en: The personal sense covers the years of youth.
branches.cn: 个人义项涵盖年少的岁月。

branches.en: The metaphor sense describes young industries.
branches.cn: 比喻义项描述年轻的行业。

branches.en: Childhood friends are friends from those years.
branches.cn: childhood friends 是那段岁月结识的朋友。

branches.en: Both senses share the image of an early beginning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「早期开端」的意象。

branches.en: A science in its childhood still makes basic mistakes.
branches.cn: 处于童年期的科学仍会犯基本错误。

intro.en: Childhood is a clean compound of a noun and a period suffix.
intro.cn: childhood 是名词与时期后缀的清晰组合。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin: child is Germanic and -hood comes from Old English -had.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语：child 属日耳曼语，-hood 来自古英语 -had。

items.meaning: the period of being a child
items.exampleCN: 他的童年塑造了他的品味。

items.example: He has a childlike trust in people.
items.exampleCN: 他对人有种孩子般天真的信任。

items.meaning: the period of being an adult
the state of being a man

latinEntries.example: Cild is the first half of childhood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cild 是 childhood 的前半。

latinEntries.example: The suffix -had became modern -hood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 后缀 -had 变成现代的 -hood。

definition_en: a small piece broken off something, a thin fried piece of potato, or a tiny electronic circuit
core_image: 一小块从木头边缘崩落的薄片
scene: 木匠的工作台上散着一层薄木片。He swept the wood chips into a small pile.
sceneCN: 这里 chip 指「碎片」（第 1 个义项：从整块上崩下的小片）；句意是他把木屑扫成一小堆。

senses.title: A small broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece that has broken off a hard material
senses.definitionCN: 从硬质材料上崩落的小片
senses.example: A chip of stone flew up from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一小块石头从路面飞起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named a piece of wood, and the sense widened to any broken fragment.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指一小片木头，后来扩展到任何碎裂的片段。

senses.title: A fried potato slice
senses.definition: a thin piece of potato fried until crisp or golden
senses.definitionCN: 切成薄片、炸至酥脆或金黄的土豆
senses.example: The children shared a bag of chips.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们分吃了一袋薯片。
senses.why: A slice of potato looks like a wood chip, so the same word was borrowed for food.
senses.whyCN: 一片土豆看起来像木片，于是同一个词被借去指食物。

senses.title: A tiny electronic circuit
senses.definition: a very small piece of silicon carrying an electronic circuit
senses.definitionCN: 承载电子电路的一小片硅
senses.example: The new chip runs twice as fast.
senses.exampleCN: 新芯片的运行速度是原来的两倍。
senses.why: A silicon wafer is cut into small pieces, and each piece kept the name chip.
senses.whyCN: 硅片被切成小块，每一块都沿用了 chip 这个名字。

intro.en: Chip began as a piece of wood and spread to food and then to electronics.
intro.cn: chip 起初指一小片木头，后来扩展到食物，再扩展到电子元件。

items.en: Cipp named a small piece of wood.
items.cn: 古英语 cipp 指一小片木头。

items.en: Chip kept the wood sense and added any broken fragment.
items.cn: 中古英语 chip 保留木片义，又添上任何碎裂片段的意思。

items.en: Chips came to name slices of fried potato.
items.cn: chips 开始指炸土豆片。

items.en: The word was applied to a tiny electronic circuit.
items.cn: 这个词被用到微型电子电路上。

items.en: Chip covers fragments, fried food and computer hardware.
items.cn: 如今 chip 涵盖碎片、油炸食品与计算机硬件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names fragments and small parts.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出碎片与小部件。

entries.definition: the part of the face below the mouth
to cut something with quick heavy blows
entries.definitionCN: 用快速有力的动作砍切

entries.definition: a small African ape
a small part broken from something
entries.definitionCN: 从某物上碎下的一小部分

entries.definition: a thin flat piece cut from something
a very small electronic circuit

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the wood origin, the fried potato sense and the silicon chip.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用木头来源、炸土豆义以及硅芯片。

normal.en: A chip is what flies off when an axe meets wood.
normal.cn: chip 就是斧头砍到木头时飞出来的那一小片。

normal.en: A potato sliced thin looks just like a wood chip, so the food took the name.
normal.cn: 切薄的土豆像极了木片，于是食物也用了这个名字。

normal.en: A computer chip is also a small cut piece, this time of silicon.
normal.cn: 计算机芯片同样是一小块切下来的东西，只不过材料是硅。

normal.en: Chip in means to add your share, money or words.
normal.cn: chip in 意为添上自己那一份，无论是钱还是话。

normal.en: The past tense chipped doubles the p before -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式 chipped 在 -ed 前双写 p。

abstract.en: Picture a pale curl of wood falling from a plane.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷浅色木屑从刨子上落下。

abstract.en: Picture a crisp golden slice lifted from hot oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一片金黄脆片从热油里被捞起。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny square of silicon held by tweezers.
abstract.cn: 想象镊子夹着一小片方形硅片。

examples.en: A chip broke off the edge of the cup.
examples.cn: 杯子边缘崩掉了一小块。

examples.en: He ordered fish and chips at the corner shop.
examples.cn: 他在街角小店点了炸鱼薯条。

examples.en: Every phone contains several chips.
examples.cn: 每部手机里都有好几块芯片。

dict_mnemonic.text: chip 就像砍木头崩下的小片：木片、薯片、芯片，都是「一小片」。

root: 源自古英语 cipp（一小片木头），属日耳曼语；后扩展指碎片、油炸土豆片与硅芯片。

sensesIntro.en: A broken wood piece is the base, a potato slice borrows the shape, and a cut silicon square borrows the size.
sensesIntro.cn: 崩落的木片是基础，土豆片借了它的形状，切下的硅片借了它的小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece flying off a hard edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：从硬物边缘飞下的一小片。

branches.en: The fragment sense covers stone and wood.
branches.cn: 碎片义项涵盖石头与木头。

branches.en: The food sense is a thin fried slice.
branches.cn: 食物义项指薄薄的油炸片。

branches.en: The technology sense is a cut silicon square.
branches.cn: 技术义项指切下的方形硅片。

branches.en: Both senses share a small flat shape.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享小而扁的形状。

branches.en: Food and hardware are both counted in chips.
branches.cn: 食物与硬件都用 chips 来计数。

intro.en: Chip stays one short stem across its plural, verb forms and compounds.
intro.cn: chip 在复数、动词形式与复合词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, with no Latin source for this small word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，这个小词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: A chip flew off the stone.

items.meaning: many small pieces or portions of food

items.example: He chipped the edge of the plate.
items.exampleCN: 他把盘子边缘磕出了缺口。

items.example: The ice was chipping under the axe.
She drank from a chipped cup.
items.exampleCN: 她用一只缺口杯子喝水。

items.meaning: board made of pressed wood chips
items.example: The shelf is made of chipboard.
items.exampleCN: 这个架子是刨花板做的。
微芯片改变了计算技术。

items.example: Cipp is the oldest form of chip.
items.exampleCN: cipp 是 chip 最古老的形式。

latinEntries.example: Cipp became modern chip.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cipp 变成现代的 chip。

definition_zh: 巧克力；巧克力糖；深褐色
definition_en: a sweet brown food made from cocoa beans, a small sweet piece of it, or the dark brown colour of it
core_image: 掰开一块排块巧克力时露出的整齐方格
scene: 桌上摊着没写完的作业，孩子偷偷伸出手。She hid a bar of chocolate under her pillow.
sceneCN: 这里 chocolate 指「巧克力」（第 1 个义项：用可可豆制成的甜食）；句意是她把一块巧克力藏在了枕头下面。

derivatives.zh: 巧克力制作师；巧克力商

senses.title: A sweet food from cocoa
senses.definition: a sweet brown food made from roasted and ground cocoa beans
senses.definitionCN: 用烘焙研磨的可可豆制成的褐色甜食
senses.example: She melted the chocolate in a small pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她用小锅把巧克力化开。
senses.why: The Aztecs drank a bitter cocoa mixture, and sugar turned that drink into the solid food we know.
senses.whyCN: 阿兹特克人喝苦涩的可可饮料，加糖后那种饮料变成了今天这种固体甜食。

senses.title: A single sweet piece
senses.definition: a small sweet made of chocolate, often with a soft filling
senses.definitionCN: 用巧克力做成的小糖果，常带柔软夹心
senses.example: He offered me a chocolate from the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他从盒子里拿了一颗巧克力给我。
senses.why: Once the food was sold in small moulded pieces, the countable piece took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这种甜食开始做成小块出售之后，可数的一块也叫同一个名字。

senses.title: A dark brown colour
senses.definition: a deep brown colour like that of plain chocolate
senses.definitionCN: 像纯巧克力那样的深褐色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm chocolate.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成了温暖的深褐色。
senses.why: The colour of the food became a colour name by direct comparison.
senses.whyCN: 食物的颜色通过直接类比变成了颜色名称。

intro.en: Chocolate comes from a Nahuatl word for a bitter cocoa drink.
intro.cn: chocolate 源出纳瓦特尔语，本指一种苦涩的可可饮料。

items.en: Xocolatl named a bitter drink made from cocoa.
items.cn: xocolatl 指用可可制成的一种苦味饮料。

items.en: Spanish explorers carried the drink home as chocolate.
items.cn: 西班牙探险者以 chocolate 之名把这种饮料带回本国。

items.en: English borrowed the Spanish word and kept its spelling.
items.cn: 英语借入这个西班牙语词，并保留了拼写。

items.en: Sugar and milk turned the drink into a solid sweet food.
items.cn: 糖与牛奶把这种饮料变成了固体甜食。

items.en: The word then named small sweets and the dark brown colour.
items.cn: 这个词随后又指小块糖果与深褐色。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps cocoa words with a similar shape, while the meaning group names sweet foods.
note.cn: 形近组列出拼写相近的可可类词，近义组列出各种甜食。

entries.definition: the brown powder left after cocoa beans are pressed
entries.definitionCN: 可可豆压榨后留下的褐色粉末

entries.definition: the coconut palm or its large nut
having the taste or smell of chocolate
entries.definitionCN: 带有巧克力味道或气味的

entries.definition: a sweet food made mainly with sugar
a small piece of sweet food eaten as a treat
entries.definitionCN: 当作小享受来吃的一小块甜食

entries.definition: a sweet food made with sugar and flavourings
entries.definitionCN: 用糖和调味料制成的甜食

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cocoa source, the bar and piece contrast, the drink and the colour.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用可可来源、排块与单颗的对比、饮料义以及颜色义。

normal.en: Chocolate keeps its Spanish shape, so the first syllable does not sound like church.
normal.cn: chocolate 保留了西班牙语的外形，所以开头并不读成 church 的音。

normal.en: Cocoa is the powder and chocolate is the food: two words grow from one bean.
normal.cn: cocoa 是粉，chocolate 是食物：一个豆子长出两个词。

normal.en: A bar is one whole block, while a chocolate is one small piece in a box.
normal.cn: a bar 是整块，a chocolate 是盒子里的一小颗。

normal.en: Hot chocolate is a drink and chocolate brown is a colour, both from the same noun.
normal.cn: hot chocolate 是饮料，chocolate brown 是颜色，都来自同一个名词。

normal.en: Chocolatier adds the agent suffix, naming the person who makes the sweets.
normal.cn: chocolatier 加上施动后缀，指做这种甜食的人。

abstract.en: Picture a dark bar snapping into even squares between two thumbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一块深色巧克力在两根拇指之间掰成整齐的方格。

abstract.en: Picture a steaming cup with a spoon of cocoa stirred in.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯冒着热气的饮料里搅进一勺可可粉。

abstract.en: Picture a winter coat in a warm brown that matches the food.
abstract.cn: 想象一件与这种食物同色的暖褐色冬衣。

examples.en: She keeps a square of chocolate for the walk home.
examples.cn: 她留着一小块巧克力，走路回家时吃。

examples.en: The shop sells chocolates with orange filling.
examples.cn: 这家店卖带橙味夹心的巧克力糖。

examples.en: His coat was a deep chocolate brown.
examples.cn: 他的外套是深巧克力褐色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cho 想成「稠」，co 想成「可」，late 想成「拉特」：稠稠的可可拉着丝，就是巧克力。

root: 源自纳瓦特尔语 xocolatl（苦涩的可可饮料），经西班牙语 chocolate 进入英语，后由饮料转为固体甜食。

sensesIntro.en: A bitter drink becomes a sweet food, then a countable piece, and finally a colour name.
sensesIntro.cn: 苦涩的饮料先变成甜食，再变出可数的一颗，最后成为颜色名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark bar breaking into neat squares.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块深色排块被掰成整齐的方格。

branches.en: The solid food grew out of the old cocoa drink.
branches.cn: 这种固体甜食从旧日的可可饮料演变而来。

branches.en: Small moulded pieces make the mass countable.
branches.cn: 做成小块之后，这种食物就可以数了。

branches.en: The colour is named straight after the food.
branches.cn: 颜色直接借这种食物来命名。

branches.en: Food and piece share one word, divided only by countability.
branches.cn: 食物与单颗共用一个词，只靠可数性区分。

branches.en: The colour sense keeps the look of the food.
branches.cn: 颜色义保留了这种食物的外观。

intro.en: One borrowed noun grows a plural, two adjectives, an agent noun and a playful compound.
intro.cn: 一个借来的名词长出复数、两个形容词、一个施动名词和一个戏谑的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word travelled from Nahuatl through Spanish, so its base is not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从纳瓦特尔语经西班牙语传来，词基并非拉丁语。

items.example: Chocolate melts quickly in a warm hand.
items.exampleCN: 巧克力在温暖的手里化得很快。
盒子里装着十二颗巧克力糖。

items.example: The sauce was rich and chocolatey.
items.exampleCN: 这酱汁浓郁，有巧克力味。

items.example: The chocolatier opened a small shop.
items.exampleCN: 这位巧克力制作师开了一家小店。
她自称嗜食巧克力的人。
choco- 出现在 chocoholic 里。

items.meaning: a person who works with something

latinEntries.example: Xocolatl was drunk cold and unsweetened.
latinEntries.exampleCN: xocolatl 当年冷饮且不加糖。

latinEntries.example: Spanish chocolate crossed into English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 西班牙语 chocolate 进入了英语。

definition_zh: 选择；选择权；可供选择的事物；精选的
definition_en: the act of picking one thing rather than another, the right to do so, or a range of things to pick from
core_image: 两扇并排的门，一只手伸向其中一扇
scene: 站在路口，风把两边的招牌吹得直晃。She had no choice but to wait for the next bus.
sceneCN: 这里 choice 指「选择」（第 1 个义项：从多个可能中挑出一个）；句意是她别无选择，只能等下一班车。

senses.title: The act of picking
senses.definition: the act of deciding between two or more possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 在两个或多个可能之间作出决定的行为
senses.example: The choice of a career took him a whole year.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了整整一年来选择职业。
senses.why: Old French choisir meant to see a difference, and picking grew out of that act of judging.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 choisir 本指看出差别，挑选便从这种判断中生长出来。

senses.title: The right to decide
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to decide what you want
senses.definitionCN: 决定自己想要什么的权利或机会
senses.example: You have a choice: pay now or pay later.
senses.exampleCN: 你有选择权：现在付还是以后再付。
senses.why: If two things are seen as different, the power to decide between them becomes something a person owns.
senses.whyCN: 一旦两样东西被看作不同，在两者之间决定的能力便成了人所拥有之物。

senses.title: A range to pick from
senses.definition: a range of things from which one may be picked
senses.definitionCN: 可供挑选的一组事物
senses.example: The shop offers a wide choice of teas.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店可供挑选的茶叶种类很多。
senses.why: The noun then named the whole set that waits to be judged.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词随后指等待被挑选的整个集合。

intro.en: Choice comes from an Old French verb that meant to see a difference.
intro.cn: choice 源出一个意为「看出差别」的古法语动词。

items.en: A Germanic root meant to perceive or to test.
items.cn: 一个日耳曼语词根意为察觉或检验。

items.en: Choisir meant to see the difference between things.
items.cn: choisir 意为看出事物之间的差别。

items.en: Chois named both the act and the result of choosing.
items.cn: chois 既指挑选的行为，也指挑选的结果。

items.en: English choice kept the act and the right to act.
items.cn: 英语 choice 保留了这一行为以及行动的权利。

items.en: The word widened to a range of goods and to the sense of select quality.
items.cn: 词义扩展到一批商品，也扩展出「精选优质」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch sound, while the meaning group names ways of deciding.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch 音，近义组列出表示决定的各种说法。

entries.definition: to pick one thing from several
to be unable to breathe
the sound a person makes when speaking
one of the things you can pick
a range of things to pick from
another possibility instead of the first one
entries.definitionCN: 替代第一个的另一种可能

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the look-alike voice, the range sense and the three fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用形近词 voice、种类义以及三个固定搭配。

normal.en: Choice and voice differ by one letter: with a voice you dare to make a choice.
normal.cn: choice 与 voice 只差一个字母：有了声音，才敢做出选择。

normal.en: Make a choice, have no choice, by choice: three phrases cover act, lack and will.
normal.cn: make a choice、have no choice、by choice，三个搭配分别覆盖行为、被迫与自愿。

normal.en: A wide choice means a large range waiting on the shelf.
normal.cn: a wide choice 指货架上等着被挑的一大片。

normal.en: Choice meat is the best cut, so the adjective means select quality.
normal.cn: choice meat 是最好的一块肉，于是形容词义为精选优质。

normal.en: The verb is choose, the noun is choice, and the adjective is choosy.
normal.cn: 动词是 choose，名词是 choice，形容词是 choosy。

abstract.en: Picture two closed doors side by side and one hand already on a handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇并排关着的门，一只手已经按在把手上。

abstract.en: Picture a long shelf of teas, each tin a little different.
abstract.cn: 想象一长排茶叶罐，每一罐都略有不同。

abstract.en: Picture a butcher pointing to the finest cut on the board.
abstract.cn: 想象肉铺老板指着案板上最好的一块肉。

examples.en: You made the right choice.
examples.cn: 你作出了正确的选择。

examples.en: The menu gives guests a choice of three soups.
examples.cn: 菜单给客人三种汤可选。

examples.en: She chose the cheaper one, and the choice pleased her.
examples.cn: 她挑了便宜的那一个，这个选择让她满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: choice 与 voice 只差一个字母：先有发声的勇气，才有选择的机会。

root: 源自日耳曼语词根，经古法语 choisir（辨别、挑选）与名词 chois 进入英语，本义是看出事物之间的差别。

sensesIntro.en: Seeing a difference gives the act of picking, then the right to pick, and finally the whole range offered.
sensesIntro.cn: 看出差别先给出挑选的行为，再给出挑选的权利，最后指摆出的整个范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for one of two offered objects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向摆出的两样东西中的一样。

branches.en: The act of picking is the first meaning of the noun.
branches.cn: 挑选的行为是这个名词的第一层意思。

branches.en: The same noun then names the power behind the act.
branches.cn: 同一个名词随后指这个行为背后的权力。

branches.en: The set of goods on offer takes the name last.
branches.cn: 摆出来供选的那批货物最后得到这个名称。

branches.en: Act and right share one word in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 在日常说法里，行为与权利共用一个词。

branches.en: A wide choice means both freedom and plenty.
branches.cn: a wide choice 同时意味着自由与充足。

intro.en: The base noun choice grows a plural, an adjective and a related verb family.
intro.cn: 名词词基 choice 长出复数、一个形容词以及一组相关动词。

latinIntro.en: Old French choisir stands behind choice, and the same stem produced choose and chosen.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 choisir 是 choice 的前身，同一词干还生出 choose 与 chosen。

items.example: Her choices shaped the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 她的选择塑造了整个团队。

items.meaning: the state of being hard to please

items.exampleCN: 你可以挑任何一个座位。

items.example: Choosing a school is never easy.
The chosen design was very simple.
items.exampleCN: 被选中的设计非常简洁。

latinEntries.meaning: to see a difference and pick
latinEntries.example: Choisir is the direct source of choice.
latinEntries.exampleCN: choisir 是 choice 的直接来源。

definition_en: to pick one thing from a group, to decide to do something, or to prefer one thing to another
core_image: 一只手伸向一堆果子里的一颗
scene: 桌上摆着两封录取通知，她迟迟没有动手。In the end she chose the smaller college.
sceneCN: 这里 chose 是 choose 的过去式，指「选择」（第 1 个义项：从多个可能中挑出一个）；句意是她最终选了那所较小的学院。

collocations.zh: 在两个工作之间作选择

senses.title: To pick from several
senses.definition: to decide which one you want from a group of things
senses.definitionCN: 从一组东西中决定要哪一个
senses.example: She chose a red scarf from the rack.
senses.exampleCN: 她从架子上挑了一条红围巾。
senses.why: Old English ceosan meant to test and approve, and approval grew into the act of picking.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ceosan 意为检验并认可，认可之后便成了挑选。

senses.title: To decide to act
senses.definition: to decide to do something after thinking about it
senses.definitionCN: 思考之后决定做某事
senses.example: He chose to walk home alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他决定一个人走回家。
senses.why: Picking an action rather than an object turned the verb into a verb of decision.
senses.whyCN: 挑的是一个动作而不是一件东西，于是这个动词也成了表示决定的词。

senses.title: To prefer one side
senses.definition: to prefer one thing or person to another
senses.definitionCN: 比起另一样更偏爱某物或某人
senses.example: You may choose tea over coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以选茶而不选咖啡。
senses.why: Comparison sharpens the sense until the verb means to favour one side.
senses.whyCN: 比较使词义更鲜明，直到这个动词表示偏向一方。

intro.en: Choose goes back to an Old English verb meaning to test and approve.
intro.cn: choose 可上溯到一个意为检验并认可的古英语动词。

items.en: The root keus- meant to taste and judge.
items.cn: 词根 keus- 意为品尝并判断。

items.en: Ceosan meant to test something and find it good.
items.cn: ceosan 意为检验某物并认为它好。

items.en: Chesen moved the stress to the act of picking.
items.cn: chesen 把重心移到挑选这个动作上。

items.en: The modern spelling choose settled beside chose and chosen.
items.cn: 现代拼写 choose 与 chose、chosen 一并固定下来。

items.en: The verb widened from objects to actions and to open preference.
items.cn: 这个动词从挑选物件扩展到决定行动与公开的偏爱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch spelling, while the meaning group names acts of selection.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch 拼写，近义组列出各种挑选的动作。

entries.definition: the act or right of picking
to run after someone to catch them
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食物

entries.definition: to pick the most suitable one
to choose one from a group
to make a choice between possibilities
entries.definitionCN: 在多种可能中作出选择

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the choice family, the irregular past forms and the three sentence patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 choice 词族、不规则过去式以及三种句型。

normal.en: Choose is the verb, choice is the noun, and chosen is the finished result.
normal.cn: choose 是动词，choice 是名词，chosen 是完成后的结果。

normal.en: The past is chose and the participle is chosen, so the long oo shortens once.
normal.cn: 过去式是 chose，过去分词是 chosen，长音 oo 会缩短一次。

normal.en: Choose between, choose from, choose to: three frames cover things, lists and actions.
normal.cn: choose between、choose from、choose to，三种框架覆盖事物、清单与动作。

normal.en: Pick and choose is the critical phrase, meaning to reject most of what is offered.
normal.cn: pick and choose 是挑剔的说法，意为把摆出来的大部分都拒掉。

normal.en: A chooser acts, while a choosy person is hard to satisfy.
normal.cn: chooser 指做选择的人，choosy 则指难以满足的人。

abstract.en: Picture fingers hovering over a bowl of fruit before closing on one.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在一碗果子上面停住，最后捏住其中一颗。

abstract.en: Picture two letters on a table and a long silence above them.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两封信，上方是一段长长的沉默。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting one book out of a crowded shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从拥挤的书架上抽出一本书。

examples.en: You can choose any colour you like.
examples.cn: 你可以挑任何喜欢的颜色。

examples.en: They chose him as captain of the team.
examples.cn: 他们选他当队长。

examples.en: Choosing is easier when the list is short.
examples.cn: 清单短的时候，挑选就容易些。

dict_mnemonic.text: choose 里藏着两个 o：两眼一扫，就把想要的那一个挑出来。

root: 源自古英语 ceosan（检验、挑选），属日耳曼语族，与德语 kiesen 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Testing and approving gives the act of picking, which extends to deciding on an action and then to open preference.
sensesIntro.cn: 检验并认可先给出挑选的行为，再扩展到决定行动，最后扩展到公开的偏爱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers closing on one fruit out of many.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在许多果子里捏住其中一颗。

branches.en: Testing an object and taking it is the first sense.
branches.cn: 检验一件东西并把它拿走，是第一层意思。

branches.en: The object can be an action, so the verb means to decide.
branches.cn: 被挑的可以是一个动作，于是这个动词表示决定。

branches.en: Two things compared produce the sense of preference.
branches.cn: 两样东西一经比较，就生出偏爱的意思。

branches.en: Both senses depend on a quiet moment of judgement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一个安静的判断时刻。

branches.en: Deciding and preferring often appear together.
branches.cn: 决定与偏爱常常一起出现。

intro.en: One Old English stem yields the verb choose, its irregular forms and the noun choice.
intro.cn: 一个古英语词干生出动词 choose、它的不规则形式以及名词 choice。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; Old English ceosan is its earliest recorded shape.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，古英语 ceosan 是其最早有记录的形式。

items.example: Choose a seat near the window.
She chooses her words with care.
She is choosing a dress now.
The chooser must live with the result.
items.exampleCN: 做选择的人必须承担结果。

items.meaning: the act or right of picking

latinEntries.example: Ceosan is the oldest recorded shape of choose.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceosan 是 choose 最早有记录的形式。

definition_en: to cut something with a heavy blow, to cut food into small pieces, or a small piece of meat cut with a rib
core_image: 一把菜刀落在砧板上，把肉剁成两半
scene: 厨房里飘着洋葱味，砧板响个不停。She chopped the onions into small pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 chopped 是 chop 的过去式，指「切碎」（第 2 个义项：把食物切成小块）；句意是她把洋葱切成了小块。

senses.title: To cut with a heavy blow
senses.definition: to cut something with a heavy blow from an axe or a large knife
senses.definitionCN: 用斧头或大刀重重砍下
senses.example: He chopped the branch off the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那根树枝从树上砍了下来。
senses.why: Middle English choppen imitated the short heavy sound of a blade striking wood.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 choppen 模仿刀刃击木时短促沉重的声音。

senses.title: To cut food small
senses.definition: to cut food into small pieces with quick heavy blows
senses.definitionCN: 用快速有力的刀法把食物切成小块
senses.example: She chopped the onions into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 她把洋葱切成了小块。
senses.why: The same short blow moved from firewood to the kitchen board.
senses.whyCN: 同样短促的砍击从木柴移到了厨房砧板。

senses.title: A piece of meat on a rib
senses.definition: a small piece of meat cut together with a rib bone
senses.definitionCN: 带肋骨一起切下的一小块肉
senses.example: We had lamb chops for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚饭吃了羊排。
senses.why: A chop is literally a piece chopped off the carcass.
senses.whyCN: chop 字面上就是从整只牲畜身上剁下来的一块。

intro.en: Chop probably began as a sound word for a short heavy blow.
intro.cn: chop 最初很可能是一个模仿短促沉重砍击的拟声词。

items.en: The shape of the word echoes a blade striking wood.
items.cn: 这个词的声音模仿刀刃击木。

items.en: Choppen meant to cut with repeated heavy blows.
items.cn: choppen 意为用反复的重击来砍。

items.en: The verb spread from firewood to meat and vegetables.
items.cn: 这个动词从木柴扩展到肉类与蔬菜。

items.en: The noun named a rib piece cut off the carcass.
items.cn: 名词指从整只牲畜上剁下的带骨肉块。

items.en: Compounds gave chopsticks, chopper and the adjective choppy.
items.cn: 复合构词又生出 chopsticks、chopper 与形容词 choppy。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the short ch spelling, while the meaning group names ways of cutting.
note.cn: 形近组保持短促的 ch 拼写，近义组列出各种切割方式。

entries.definition: a small piece broken off something
a place where goods are sold
to crack or redden from cold
to divide something with a blade
to cut into thin flat pieces
to cut food into very small bits
entries.definitionCN: 把食物切成极小的碎末

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the sound of the blade, the kitchen board and the meat sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刀声、厨房砧板以及排骨义。

normal.en: Say chop twice quickly and you hear an axe on a log.
normal.cn: 快速连说两次 chop，就听见斧头落在木头上的声音。

normal.en: Chop wood is the wood sense, chop onions is the kitchen sense, and both are short blows.
normal.cn: chop wood 是劈柴义，chop onions 是厨房义，两者都是短促的砍击。

normal.en: A pork chop is a piece chopped off, so the noun keeps the verb image.
normal.cn: a pork chop 就是剁下来的一块，名词保留了动词的意象。

normal.en: Chop down adds down, and the tree falls in the direction of the blow.
normal.cn: chop down 加上 down，树便朝砍击的方向倒下。

normal.en: Chopsticks and chopper both start from the same short stem.
normal.cn: chopsticks 与 chopper 都从同一个短词干出发。

abstract.en: Picture a blade biting into a log with a dull thud.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃咬进木头，发出一声闷响。

abstract.en: Picture a board covered with neat piles of diced onion.
abstract.cn: 想象砧板上是一小堆一小堆切好的洋葱丁。

abstract.en: Picture a thick chop bone showing at the edge of the meat.
abstract.cn: 想象肉块边缘露出一截粗大的骨头。

examples.en: He chopped wood for the fire all morning.
examples.cn: 他整个上午都在劈柴生火。

examples.en: Add two chopped carrots to the pot.
examples.cn: 往锅里加两根切碎的胡萝卜。

examples.en: The pork chop was thick and juicy.
examples.cn: 那块猪排又厚又多汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: chop 读起来就像刀落砧板的一声：剁。

root: 源自中古英语 choppen（砍、剁），可能模仿刀斧砍击的声音，与 chap 相关。

sensesIntro.en: A short heavy blow gives the cutting sense, which moves to the kitchen and then to the piece of meat cut off.
sensesIntro.cn: 短促的重击先给出砍的动作，再移到厨房，最后指剁下来的那块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade falling once on a wooden board.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃在木板上落下一次。

branches.en: The axe sense is the oldest and the most physical.
branches.cn: 斧头义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: The same blow works on onions and carrots.
branches.cn: 同样的砍击用在洋葱与胡萝卜上。

branches.en: The noun names the piece that the blow leaves.
branches.cn: 名词指这一刀之后留下的那块肉。

branches.en: Wood and food share one verb of short strokes.
branches.cn: 木柴与食物共用一个短促下刀的动词。

branches.en: The cut food and the cut meat sit side by side.
branches.cn: 切好的菜与剁下的肉彼此相邻。

intro.en: The short stem chop carries the verb, its inflections and three familiar compounds.
intro.cn: 短词干 chop 支撑动词、各种屈折形式以及三个常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and partly imitative, so no Latin root is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语且带拟声成分，不涉及拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to cut with a heavy blow

items.example: The chopper hung by the stove.
The lake was choppy that day.
He ate the noodles with chopsticks.

latinEntries.example: Choppen is the recorded source of chop.
latinEntries.exampleCN: choppen 是 chop 有记录的来源。

definition_zh: 扔；抛；丢弃；放弃；卡盘；夹头；（口语）轻拍
definition_en: to throw something carelessly, to discard or give up something, or a device that clamps and holds a tool or workpiece in a machine
core_image: 随手一抛：东西没被郑重地放下，而是被轻轻甩了出去
scene: 工间休息时，工人看见口袋里的碎纸团。He opened his fist and gave the paper a careless chuck into the bin.
sceneCN: 这里 chuck 是名词「随手一抛」（第 4 个义项：不经意的投掷动作）；句意是他张开手掌，把纸团随随便便抛进垃圾桶，突出动作的随意和不郑重。

derivatives.zh: 由 chuck（路面）+ hole（洞）构成，义为「路面坑洼」（美式口语）
由 chuck 加昵称后缀构成，义为「小鸡」（儿语）
由 chuck 与 full 构成的变体，义为「塞得满满的」（美国方言）

senses.title: To throw something carelessly
senses.definition: to throw something in a casual or careless way
senses.definitionCN: 随意地、不太郑重地把某物扔出或抛出
senses.example: She chucked her coat on the bed and flopped down beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 她把外套往床上一扔，一屁股躺倒在旁边。
senses.why: The core image is a light, unceremonious toss: the arm flicks and the object flies, with no care about where it lands.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是轻巧随意的抛掷：手臂一甩东西就飞出去，完全不在乎落在哪里，所以最早的动词义就是「随手扔」。

senses.title: To discard or get rid of something
senses.definition: to throw something away because you do not want it any more
senses.definitionCN: 把不要的东西处理掉、丢弃
senses.example: These old shoes are finished—just chuck them out.
senses.exampleCN: 这双旧鞋没法穿了，直接扔掉吧。
senses.why: If tossing is careless, the natural next step is tossing into the bin: the throw becomes a deliberate act of disposal.
senses.whyCN: 既然「扔」是不经意的，往垃圾桶一扔就成了主动丢弃：投掷动作延伸为「处理掉不要的东西」。

senses.title: To give up a job, plan, or relationship
senses.definition: to give up or abandon something such as a job or a plan, often suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然或干脆地放弃工作、计划或关系
senses.example: After one terrible month, he chucked the job and went travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 过了糟糕的一个月，他干脆辞了职去旅行。
senses.why: Discarding a thing extends metaphorically to discarding commitments: you 'throw away' the job or plan as if it were rubbish.
senses.whyCN: 丢掉物品的意象投射到抽象层面：把工作或计划像垃圾一样「一扔了之」，于是引申出放弃、辞掉之义。

senses.title: A casual throw; the act of tossing
senses.definition: an act of throwing something lightly or carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 一次轻率随意的抛掷动作
senses.example: With a quick chuck of the ball, the game started.
senses.exampleCN: 球被随手一抛，比赛就开始了。
senses.why: The action verb is converted into a noun naming the action itself, a very common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词指称动作本身，这是英语里极常见的用法，「扔一下」变成「一抛」这个名词。

senses.title: A clamping device in a machine
senses.definition: a device on a lathe or drill that grips the tool or the workpiece tightly
senses.definitionCN: 车床或钻床上夹紧刀具或工件的装置
senses.example: Loosen the chuck before you change the drill bit.
senses.exampleCN: 换钻头之前先松开卡盘。
senses.why: Another chuck word, of different origin, means a grip or clamp; mechanics borrowed it for the device that 'bites' and holds the tool.
senses.whyCN: 机械领域借用了另一个来源的 chuck（咬合、夹持），指那种像嘴巴一样咬紧刀具的夹持装置，与「扔」义只是拼写巧合。

senses.title: A cut of beef from the shoulder
senses.definition: a cut of meat from the lower neck and shoulder of a cow
senses.definitionCN: 牛颈部下方与肩部之间切下的一块肉
senses.example: Chuck makes a rich stew because it has just enough fat.
senses.exampleCN: 牛肩肉脂肪适中，炖出来的汤很浓郁。
senses.why: This sense again comes from a separate chuck word meaning a piece or cut, showing how one spelling gathers several unrelated histories.
senses.whyCN: 这一义来自另一个意为「一块、一份」的 chuck，说明同一个拼写背后聚着几条互不相干的词源线索。

senses.title: To pat or touch someone playfully
senses.definition: to tap someone gently, especially under the chin, as an affectionate gesture
senses.definitionCN: 亲昵地轻拍某人，尤指轻托下巴
senses.example: Grandmother gave the baby a playful chuck under the chin.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母亲昵地轻托了一下宝宝的下巴。
senses.why: A gentle, playful movement sits close to a light throw in feeling, so the same casual word covers this affectionate tap.
senses.whyCN: 轻巧、玩闹的动作与「轻抛」在感觉上很接近，同一个随意的词便也覆盖了这种亲昵的轻拍。

senses.title: To utter a clucking sound; to cluck
senses.definition: to make a short clucking sound, as a hen does, or to call chickens with such a sound
senses.definitionCN: 发出类似母鸡的咯咯短促叫声，或用这种声音唤鸡
senses.example: The old hen chuck-chucked whenever strangers came near.
senses.exampleCN: 只要有生人靠近，老母鸡就咯咯地叫个不停。
senses.why: This is likely an imitative word, echoing the hen's call directly; it is probably yet another separate chuck.
senses.whyCN: 这一义很可能是拟声词，直接模仿母鸡的叫声，多半又是一条独立的 chuck 词源线索。

intro.en: Chuck is a spelling that gathers several distinct histories: a casual-throw verb of uncertain deeper origin, a separate clamp word, a meat-cut term, and an imitation of a hen's call.
intro.cn: chuck 这个拼写背后聚着几条互不相干的历史：一条来源不深的「随手扔」动词线索、一条独立的「夹持」线索、一块肉的名称，以及对母鸡叫声的模仿。

items.en: The verb chukken appears in Middle English meaning to throw carelessly and also to cluck like a hen; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it may be imitative or related to chick.
items.cn: 中古英语出现动词 chukken，既表「随手扔」，也表「咯咯叫」；更深来源不确定，一般认为可能是拟声，或与 chick（小鸡）相关。

items.en: The affectionate use develops: to chuck someone means to pat them gently, and Chuck becomes a familiar nickname for Charles, from terms of endearment for a 'darling'.
items.cn: 亲昵用法发展起来：chuck someone 表示轻轻拍打，Chuck 又成为 Charles 的昵称，源于表示「心肝宝贝」的爱称。

items.en: A separate chuck meaning 'a grip, a bite' appears in dialect; machinists later adopt it for the clamping device, giving the technical sense of drill chuck.
items.cn: 方言中出现另一个意为「咬合、夹持」的 chuck；机械工匠后来用它称呼夹紧装置，于是有了钻夹头这一技术义。

items.en: The noun chuck names a cut of beef from the neck and shoulder, generally thought to come from the same dialect word for a piece or chunk of meat.
items.cn: 名词 chuck 开始指牛颈肩部切下的一块肉，一般认为来自方言中表示「一块肉」的同一个词。

items.en: Phrasal verbs multiply in colloquial speech: chuck up (give up), chuck out (discard, expel), chuck in (add casually), making the verb a workhorse of informal English.
items.cn: 口语中短语动词大量出现：chuck up（放弃）、chuck out（扔掉、赶出）、chuck in（顺手加上），使这个动词成为非正式英语里的多用词。

items.en: Today chuck covers casual throwing, disposal, giving up, the machine clamp, the meat cut, and the chicken's call—several histories hiding under one short spelling.
items.cn: 今天 chuck 同时涵盖随手扔、丢弃、放弃、机械卡盘、牛肩肉和母鸡叫声——一个短短的拼写之下藏着好几条历史线索。

note.en: Chuck hides several word histories under one spelling, so look-alikes come from different roots, and near-meaning words cluster around casual throwing and discarding.
note.cn: chuck 一个拼写下藏着多条词源线索，所以形近词常来自不同词根，而近义词则围绕「随手扔、丢弃」这个义场聚集。

entries.definition: a young bird, especially a young chicken

normalIntro.en: Build the memory from sound, spelling, phrasal verbs and real usage.
normalIntro.cn: 从发音、拼写、短语动词和真实用法几个角度搭记忆。

normal.cn: chuck away 与 throw away 结构完全平行，把它记成「双份的扔掉」即可。

normal.en: In the workshop, the chuck grips the drill bit—picture a mechanical hand that 'bites' the tool.
normal.cn: 在车间里，卡盘咬住钻头——想象一只机械手把工具紧紧咬住。

normal.en: At the butcher's, ask for chuck beef: the shoulder cut that stews well.
normal.cn: 在肉铺要 chuck beef：炖汤好吃的牛肩肉。

normal.en: Nickname memory: Chuck is the friendly short form of Charles—an informal word for an informal set of meanings.
normal.cn: 昵称记忆：Chuck 是 Charles 的随和简称——一个随意的词配一整套随意义项。

abstract.cn: 想象一把扫过桌面：文件、计划和烦恼统统被抛进垃圾桶。

abstract.en: Picture a machine jaw snapping shut—tight, precise, the exact opposite of a careless throw.
abstract.cn: 想象机械钳口咔哒合拢——紧而精准，恰是「随手一扔」的反面。

abstract.en: Hear the hen's chuck-chuck in the yard: the same short syllable clucking in the morning air.
abstract.cn: 听院子里母鸡咯咯的叫声：同一个短音节在清晨的空气里回响。

examples.en: He chucked the ball to his brother and ran to first base.

examples.en: Tighten the chuck firmly, or the drill bit will slip.
examples.cn: 把卡盘拧紧，否则钻头会打滑。

examples.en: She chucked everything into a suitcase and left for the airport.
examples.cn: 她把所有东西一股脑塞进箱子就动身去机场了。

root: 一般认为 chuck（扔）是中古英语 chukken 的延续，深层来源不确定，可能是拟声或与 chick（小鸡）同源；机械义的卡盘与牛肉义的牛肩肉来自另外两条独立的 chuck 线索（方言「咬合、夹持」与「一块肉」），存疑处已在词源部分标注。

sensesIntro.en: From a careless throw, the meanings fan out into disposal, giving up, the noun for the throw itself, and then into the unrelated clamp, meat-cut, pat and cluck senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「随手一扔」出发，词义先扩散为丢弃、放弃和指称抛掷动作本身的名词，再接入互不相干的卡盘、牛肩肉、轻拍与咯咯叫诸义。

senses.title: A service of worship

senses.exampleCN: 他们每个星期日都去做礼拜。

intro.en: Church descends from a Greek phrase meaning the house of the Lord.
intro.cn: church 源出一个意为「主的房屋」的希腊语说法。

items.en: Kyriakon meant the house belonging to the Lord.
items.cn: kyriakon 意为属于主的房屋。

items.cn: 这个词以 kirika 的形式在日耳曼语族群中向北传播。

items.en: Cirice named the building and the community together.
items.cn: cirice 同时指建筑与群体。

items.en: Chirche settled into the modern sound and spelling.
items.cn: chirche 固定为现代的读音与拼写。

items.cn: 这个词同时保留建筑、群体与仪式三层意思。
